verdicts.reason: Quote supports it. Actor should be the FIFO/DUT rather than slave; flag is checkable every cycle from interface signals (i_wr_en, full, o_overflow).

Stated by quote. Actor is the FIFO, not slave. Storage and write pointer are internal, so not every-cycle checkable from interface signals; use scenario (write then read back, check data/count unchanged).
Self-clear after one cycle and clear by i_rst_n_wr are stated. Actor should be the FIFO. Checkable via interface signals.
Stated. Actor should be the FIFO; checkable from interface signals.
Stated. Actor is the FIFO. The read pointer is internal; o_rd_data holding its value is observable but needs a data-aware check, so scenario.
Stated. Actor should be the FIFO; checkable from interface signals.

Quote says single-domain reset leaves inconsistent state that is not detected and recovery is to reset both; this is an integrator responsibility. The 'must' is fine, but nothing is verifiable on the IP; keep as none with strength MUST on integrator.

The quote says the IP does not detect illegal parameters and behavior is undefined; it does not state a prohibition. 'Fix the configuration' is a recovery action for the integrator. Strength is SHOULD rather than MUST_NOT; nothing is verifiable.
Stated. Actor should be the FIFO. The no-acceptance and no-pulse parts are checkable from interface signals, but the software-reset blocking state needs the FSM, so scenario.
Stated by quote. Actor should be the FIFO/reset controller, not slave. Scenario is appropriate.
The quote only describes precedence: the flags are in different domains and do not interact. It is a description with no concrete verifiable behavior beyond what the other rules cover.

The quote says a simultaneous write and read cannot produce both errors for the same event. This is a consequence of the design (full and empty are exclusive in depth ≥ 2), not a separate requirement. It is also weaker than a MUST_NOT.
Quote uses 'shall' for the producer or consumer to react to flags, which is an external responsibility. Nothing is checkable on the IP. The actor is the system/environment; keep check none.

questions.question: Is o_overflow/o_underflow asserted in the cycle after the rejected request, or in the same cycle as the request? 'Registered, in the cycle after' needs the exact cycle relative to the clock edge sampling i_wr_en/i_rd_en.
Can a write be rejected as full while a simultaneous read frees a slot in the same cycle? The spec does not state whether full is evaluated before the read is considered.
Does a software reset block (ERR-005) also suppress o_overflow/o_underflow pulses already pending from a request just before the reset begins?
